To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relaxase domain (36 kDa) of F factor Trai was overexpressed in E. coli, crystallized, and the crystals diffract to 3.1A.

the relaxase domain TraI of the F factor is a novel type of nucleic-acid-binding protein that binds to a specific DNA sequence and cleaves the phosphodiester bond between G and A nucleotides in a single-stranded DNA.

the relaxase domain TraI of the conjugative plsmid F factor has been crystallized to a high enough resolution to allow the determination of the three-dimensional structure of the protein by X-ray diffraction methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the F factor TraI protein, which is the relaxase of the F factor.
the structure of TraI and its interaction with DNA, and the structure of the TraI-DNA complex will provide the first atomic-level understanding of a site-specific relaxase.
understanding the mechanisms by which conjugative plasmids transfer themselves between bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TraI is the first relaxase for which the crystal structure has been solved.
the crystals are of high quality.

the crystals are of the trigonal space group P3(1)21 or P3(2)21 with cell parameters a = 76.6 A, c = 110.6 A, and alpha = beta = 90 degrees, gamma = 120 degrees, and contain one molecule per asymmetric unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relaxase domain TraI is a promising target for structural studies of the F-factor conjugative plasmids and the mechanism of conjugative DNA transfer.
crystals of the 36kDa fragment of TraI were successfully obtained and characterized.
we have obtained crystals of the 36kDa N-terminal fragment (residues 1-336) of TraI that diffract to 3.1A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain high-resolution diffraction of the 36kDa TraI fragment, which will allow us to determine its structure.
it is possible to obtain high-resolution diffraction of crystals containing divalent cations and chloride salts by soaking the crystals in ethylene glycol prior to freezing.
crystals of a 36 kDa fragment of the relaxase TraI can be grown in a reproducible manner and diffract well.
